channel.title: The Git Reporter
channel.description: A code-native newspaper of meaningful software change.

item.title: The Last Click Shouldn’t Redirect an Automation
item.description: OpenWork has stopped a scheduled Automation from silently following whichever workspace a person activated last; a job can now carry its intended place with it.

item.title: API Discovery: Tool Calls Need a Home in the Stream
item.description: Pydantic AI’s public AG-UI adapter now gives a tool-only response an announced assistant-message parent—useful when a frontend rebuilds a conversation from streamed events.

item.title: Codex Says It Stopped Wasting Your Allowance. The Public Code Can Prove Only Part of It
item.description: Eight fixes, five public code trails and three closed rooms: OpenAI's repository strongly supports several mechanisms in its Codex usage announcement, but not the reset, the savings percentages or every background worker.

item.title: A Restricted Workspace Should Not Start Its Own Tools
item.description: Gemini CLI now gives an explicitly restricted or untrusted workspace a narrower configuration path: repository-defined tools, MCP servers, policies and telemetry no longer accompany its A2A server into startup.

item.title: Pydantic AI Opens Its Durable Engine to Other Runtimes
item.description: Pydantic AI has published a durable-execution backend surface for third-party workflow engines—useful when an agent needs recovery without every integration rebuilding the model, tool and capability loop.

item.title: The Old Proxy Is Gone. OpenWork's Cloud Has One Door Now.
item.description: OpenWork has deleted its standalone cloud-worker proxy; the public replacement makes a fresh signed preview the access-resolution seam while keeping a stable route for clients that cannot hold an expiring address.

item.title: Before Docker Reads the File
item.description: Headlong’s Docker broker is treating the pre-render Compose file as an authority boundary—because a path is no longer safe to inspect after the renderer has already opened it.

item.title: Headlong Makes the Parser Part of the Sandbox
item.description: The reusable craft in Headlong’s Docker-broker work is simple to state and hard to fake: validate configuration before a trusted resolver can turn it into host access.

item.title: A Shared Terminal Is Not Shared Permission
item.description: OpenClaw’s new terminal-input path separates an agent being allowed to see an operator’s terminal from being allowed to send a keystroke into it.

item.title: OpenWorker's Security Bet Starts Below the Model
item.description: OpenWorker 0.2.0 adds three security coworkers, but the source reveals something more useful than another scan button: auditable runbooks that separate scanners, model judgment, approvals, and fixes.

item.title: Perplexity Put the Cloud Behind a Permission Prompt
item.description: Portable Computer keeps its model, harness, conversation, and task trail on the user's machine by default, then asks before one step uses the web or a frontier model. That boundary matters more than its vendor-run benchmark.

item.title: Codex Puts a Broker Between the Agent and the Secret
item.description: A newly merged Codex change says a project file can describe the work, but it should not be able to switch on the credential broker or choose the provider context that reaches an agent shell.

item.title: Builder Work: CrewAI Keeps the Speaker Labels
item.description: CrewAI’s public Claude Code-assisted repair treats a conversation as ordered typed data—not a paragraph to be reassembled—and tests every path that could quietly change who said what.

item.title: Headlong Keeps the Agent Running After the Prompt Ends
item.description: Headlong says a persistent agent never sleeps. Its launch-week code shows the harder truth: continuity is a wake clock, a spend policy, one shared life log, and a rule for deciding whether a thought counts as work.

item.title: Unsloth Built a Benchmark That Can Veto Its Own Speed Claims
item.description: The new StudioBench is designed to make a performance result fail before it makes a flattering headline.

item.title: Builder Work: Mastra Makes One Agent Run Share Its Memory Reads
item.description: A cache becomes reliable when it shares only the reads that belong together—and yields to the live write that does not.

item.title: Before Cline Replaces an Agent Hub, It Starts Saying No
item.description: Cline’s Hub can now refuse new mutable work, wait for accepted sessions to settle, and replay a durable event stream to reconnecting clients before an upgrade swaps the service underneath them.

item.title: API Discovery: A Running Foundry Agent Can Take a Course Correction
item.description: Microsoft Agent Framework’s preview Foundry Hosting source adds an opt-in that lets an in-flight conversation queue a second input instead of treating it as a lock error.

item.title: Builder Work: The Model Belongs to the Session, Not the Settings File
item.description: Qwen Code’s agent-assisted daemon patch turns a fragile global preference into a tested per-session record—and offers a durable-state lesson other builders can steal.

item.title: A Release Should Not Fetch Its Rules From a Moving Main
item.description: OpenClaw is making a narrow release promise: when the product is frozen, the workflow allowed to publish it must stay identifiable even after main changes.

item.title: Qwen Code Saves the Shape of a Finished Workflow
item.description: Qwen Code is teaching a finished multi-agent run to leave behind a reviewable shape—rather than a pile of logs that dies with the terminal.

item.title: Cline Lets an Agent Schedule Work—But Not Anywhere It Likes
item.description: Cline's new durable task system lets an agent make work recur after the chat ends, but its public implementation keeps asking the harder question: which workspace gave that job authority?

item.title: Pi's New Harness Writes the Restart Point Before It Acts
item.description: Pi's dev branch is turning an agent run into a durable, remotely attachable session—but its most important promise is also the simplest: record the restart point before the model or tool gets to act.

item.title: An Approval Must Keep Its Denials
item.description: Codex is tightening the rules beneath its approval layer: a broad remembered grant must not reopen a denied child path, an unfamiliar shell must identify itself, and a stale reviewer score should be visible as stale.

item.title: An Agent Can’t Review the Wrong Tree
item.description: Qwen Code has made a workflow subagent’s linked worktree part of the job itself—a small API change with a large warning for anyone resuming, reviewing, or testing code across branches.

item.title: API Discovery: Cloudflare’s Gateway Keeps Native Agent APIs Intact
item.description: Cloudflare’s public Responses and Messages endpoints give agent builders a choice that generic gateway adapters often erase: keep the provider-shaped request format that the workflow actually needs.

item.title: Builder Work: Hermes Keeps an SDK Upgrade From Dropping the Conversation
item.description: A public Claude-assisted MCP migration in Hermes Agent shows the durable craft: make a compatibility seam explicit, then test every way an upgrade can lose meaning without crashing.

item.title: When a Context Limit Drops the User’s Turn
item.description: OpenClaw found a required Codex compaction preflight treating an intentional no-op as a fatal failure—so an overlong session could lose the incoming user turn before the model ever answered.

item.title: API Discovery: Pi’s xAI Route Keeps Reasoning State in Play
item.description: Pi now sends every built-in xAI model through the Responses API—a useful route for agents that need a deliberate, client-owned continuity plan rather than a model-name swap.

item.title: Builder Work: A Test Double Is a Contract
item.description: Unsloth’s agent-assisted CI repair shows a durable testing move: put a shared fake at the same interface boundary as production, then make the test harness reveal the task that actually failed.
